extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A public dataset pairing 3D non-contrast chest CT volumes with corresponding radiology text reports, used to develop CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bemhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, and Bjoem Menze
extraction.publisher: Istanbul Medipol University / University of Zurich / ETH Zurich
extraction.citeAs: Hamamci IE, Er S, Wang C, et al. Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated from chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. Non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023 were included. Reports were anonymized, translated from Turkish to English, and reviewed/corrected by bilingual final-year medical students. For label extraction, 1,000 reports were manually annotated for 18 abnormalities and a text classifier was finetuned to label the remaining reports.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that the second external validation set (UPMC) lacks publicly available detailed metadata, but missing data within CT-RATE itself is not explicitly described beyond excluding contrast-enhanced scans and non-chest scans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chest CT volumes and radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital; reports included clinical information, technique, findings, and impression sections.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing personal information and date-related identifiers, translated from Turkish to English using Google Translate API, and corrected by bilingual medical students. CT volumes were standardized by orientation checks, conversion to Hounsfield Units using intercept and slope metadata, clipping HU values to [-1000, 1000], and normalization to [-1, 1] during training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Volumes with contrast material or non-chest body parts were excluded. CT volumes were resized to uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in x/y and 1.5 mm in z, then center-cropped or padded to 480×480×240. Reports were anonymized and translated to English. For label extraction, findings and impression sections were merged for manual annotation and classifier training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1,000 reports were manually annotated for 18 abnormalities by merging findings and impression sections. These annotations were used to finetune a pretrained language model (RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m) to automatically extract abnormality labels from the remaining reports. The dataset also includes organ-level anatomical segmentation labels generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Google Translate API was used for translation; no dedicated human-annotation platform is explicitly named. Automated label extraction used RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, and segmentation labels were generated with TotalSegmentator.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The manually annotated reports were split into 80% training and 20% validation for the label extractor. The finetuned text encoder achieved reported precision, recall, and F1 scores for each abnormality. The paper also notes that conditions not referenced in either findings or impression were considered absent.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 label set per report for the manually annotated subset; 18 abnormalities per report.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students; no further demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, CXR-Bert, CT-ViT, TotalSegmentator, Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.1 70B
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, trained models, and code are publicly released via Hugging Face and GitHub. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age, sex, and geographic/clinical setting information are present in the dataset metadata and cohort description. Reports and metadata were anonymized before release.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to improve medical imaging AI for 3D chest CT, potentially reducing radiologist workload, improving diagnostic accuracy, and supporting patient care.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors state that the dataset is single-institution and from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may introduce bias and limit generalizability.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Single-center dataset may limit generalization to other populations; CT-CLIP depends on report terminology and prompt choice; CT-CHAT benchmarking is limited by the lack of pretrained 3D multimodal baselines; current models are limited to chest CT volumes and are not ready for clinical deployment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, zero-shot detection, finetuning, retrieval, visual question answering, and report generation.
